rules.description: New York security breach notification (General Business Law 899-aa)

individuals.standard: in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay

regulator.body: New York Attorney General, Department of State and Division of State Police (and the Department of Financial Services for covered entities)
regulator.standard: notify as to the timing, content and distribution of the notices and the approximate number of affected persons, with a copy of the notice template

consumerReportingAgencies.standard: notify consumer reporting agencies when more than five thousand New York residents are notified at one time

source.title: New York General Business Law section 899-AA

versions.notes: Subd. 2: disclosure 'in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' and 'within thirty days after the breach has been discovered'; subd. 4 law-enforcement delay; subd. 8(a) notices to the Attorney General, Department of State and Division of State Police; subd. 8(b) consumer reporting agencies where more than 5,000 residents. effectiveFrom = latest revision date shown on nysenate.gov (2025-03-28); earlier versions not modelled. The duty of a person maintaining data it does not own was not verified.

Local ordinances not yet modelled: Westchester County Earned Sick Leave, NY Paid Family Leave, NY Paid Prenatal Leave, NYC Fair Workweek.
